Intensity \(c^r x^r\) follows from independent absence probabilities, and Poisson arrival-time tails follow. A standard-library verifier passes 600 exact independent finite cross-checks. Fixed-r weak convergence only.

originality.rationale: The closest source with exactly the same statistic, arXiv:2208.03658v1, proves a generating function for aggregate r-chain mex and poses asymptotic investigation, not a rare-event onset process. The follow-up arXiv:2312.02620v1 contains bijective identities; inspected primary theorem statements and relevant proofs do not cover the Poisson onset. Classical independent-process approximation is a technique, not a theorem with these parameters. Indexed mathematical-record similarity searches produced nearest theorems on multiplicity-deficient single parts and separate missing congruence classes, both different events. Searches cannot certify absolute novelty.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently described consecutive-absence Poisson theorem might exist; negative searches are not novelty certification.
The 1994 independent-process framework is general and a broader latent corollary might be derived with work; it is not presented there as the exact r-chain theorem.
Some recent analogous papers were checked at abstract/index level only, but their definitions explicitly differ.

value.rationale: The r-chain first absent block is an explicitly motivated number-theoretic partition statistic. Its new \(n^{r/[2(r+1)]}\) scale and full inhomogeneous Poisson arrival process determine a hierarchy of rare gap locations, not just a single average or arbitrary finite invariant, and distinguish chain absence from multiplicity threshold gaps.
